MIST_AGE.SplitModulesActive: The Mist Age - Toolkit replaces {modules}. Disable those modules in Manage Modules, otherwise the toolkit stays off.

DeathLoot.Name: Loot from fallen adversaries
DeathLoot.Hint: When an adversary that carries inventory items or gold is downed (all Hit Points marked, or Dead / Defeated), its token becomes an Item Piles loot pile. It turns back if the adversary recovers.

Setting.Name: Money button for adversaries
Setting.Hint: A button in an adversary's inventory, seen by the GM only, that rolls the money it carries from the money table and adds it to its gold.

Table.Name: Money table
Table.Hint: Name of the roll table the money button rolls. Its Daggerheart roll formulas are the wealth levels to choose from; the inline rolls in the drawn result (such as [[/r 2d6 # Silver]]) are the amount, in the currency named after #.

AdversaryMoney.Tooltip: Roll money from {table} and add it to the gold

Dialog.Title: Money: {name}
Dialog.Hint: How wealthy is this adversary? The amount is rolled and added to its gold.

AdversaryMoney.NoTable: No roll table named "{table}". Set its name in the toolkit settings (Adversaries).
AdversaryMoney.NoMoney: The result "{result}" of {table} has no money rolls, such as [[/r 2d6 # Silver]].
AdversaryMoney.UnknownCurrency: Unknown currency "{currency}" in the money table.
AdversaryMoney.BadFormula: Could not roll "{formula}" from the money table.

TokenNames.Name: Token names match their sheets
TokenNames.Hint: A token shows the same name on the map, in chat, in combat and on its sheet. Linked tokens and the prototype take the actor name; an unlinked token keeps a name given to it alone, otherwise it takes the actor name. Renaming an actor, a token or a token's sheet renames the rest. Turn this off to name tokens by hand.
TokenNames.Synced: Token names now match their sheets: {count} renamed.

Ammo.AmmunitionHint: Consumables this weapon shoots. Drop them here from a compendium or from an inventory; every stack taken from the same compendium entry counts. Each attack spends one unit of one of them.
Ammo.NoneLeft: {weapon}: no ammunition left, none was spent.
Ammo.OnlyConsumables: Only consumables can be weapon ammunition.

Setting.Name: Weapon jams
Setting.Hint: Weapons that consume ammunition get a jam die and a number of jam dice. The GM requests jam rolls and raises jam dice from the Daggerheart Menu; Weapon Care on a rest sets the dice back to 1.

Jam.NoPlayers: No player with a character is online.

Raise.Title: Raise jam die
Raise.Hint: Every weapon that consumes ammunition carried by the chosen characters gets one more jam die.
Raise.NoCharacters: No character carries a weapon that consumes ammunition.

Roll.Title: Weapon Jam Roll
Roll.Hint: Choose the weapons to roll for. A 1 on any jam die of a weapon jams it.
Roll.NoWeapons: {actor} carries no weapon that consumes ammunition.

Jam.EffectHint: This weapon is jammed. Use its Clear Weapon Jam action to fix it.
Jam.ClearActionHint: Clear the jam of this weapon. Mark 1 Stress.

Care.Name: Weapon Care
Care.shortRest: Choose one weapon that consumes ammunition: its jam dice go back to 1.
Care.longRest: All weapons that consume ammunition: their jam dice go back to 1.

Setting.Name: Exhaustion checks
Setting.Hint: The GM can ask players for exhaustion checks from the Daggerheart Menu: a Strength roll against a difficulty that starts at 15 and rises with each check until the next long rest.

SheetButtonSetting.Name: Exhaustion button on character sheets
SheetButtonSetting.Hint: A button next to the rest buttons lets the sheet's owner, or the GM for a player who is offline, roll the exhaustion check. When off, checks come only from the GM's requests in the Daggerheart Menu.

Exhaustion.NoPlayers: No player with a character is online.

Request.Title: Request exhaustion checks
Request.Hint: Each chosen player rolls their own check.
Request.QuietDay: Quiet day (no events or battles): advantage on the first check since the long rest

Reset.Title: Reset exhaustion
Reset.Hint: Set every character's exhaustion difficulty back to 15, as after a long rest?

Exhaustion.EffectHint: The difficulty of the next exhaustion check. A long rest clears it.

Result.HitPoints: Marked {count} Hit Points instead of Stress.

Sheet.QuietDay: Was it a quiet day, without events or battles? By the exhaustion rules the first check since the long rest then has advantage.

Reminder.Name: Long rest reminder
Reminder.Hint: Shown at the top of the long rest dialog, for example to mark off a Ration. Leave empty to show nothing.

EmptyConsumables.Name: Remove used-up consumables
EmptyConsumables.Hint: A consumable at quantity 0 disappears from the inventory at once and is deleted when the GM next loads the world. Until then its chat card can still apply the healing or effects it rolled. Item Piles merchants keep empty stacks.

Menu.Name: Toolkit settings
Menu.Label: Open settings
Menu.Hint: Currencies, carrying capacity, overload, inventory, weapon jams, token names and adversary loot, grouped into sections.

prices.Label: Currency
prices.Hint: Exchange rates between Daggerheart currencies. Prices are stored in handfuls.

capacity.Label: Carrying capacity
capacity.Hint: Character capacity = base + Strength × per-point step (the negative step below 0). With the defaults: Strength -1 = 8, 0 = 10, 1 = 14, 2 = 18, 3 = 22 slots; a backpack adds 10 by an effect on flags.mist-age-weight.bonusSlots.

overload.Label: Overload
overload.Hint: What happens when a character carries more than its capacity: light overload is a warning, heavy overload is the full penalty.

inventory.Label: Inventory
inventory.Hint: Items in character and NPC inventories.

exhaustion.Label: Exhaustion
exhaustion.Hint: Exhaustion checks requested by the GM.

tokens.Label: Tokens
tokens.Hint: Names of tokens on the map.

MIST_AGE_PRICES.TableApplied: Price table applied: {compendium} items in world compendiums, {copies} items in the world.
MIST_AGE_PRICES.TablesRelinked: Roll tables now point to HB items: {count} results.

coinsPerHandful.Name: Rate: coins per handful
coinsPerHandful.Hint: How many coins make one handful. In The Mist Age: 10 Penny = 1 Silver. Prices are stored in handfuls, so changing a rate changes how prices split into coins, not the prices themselves.

handfulsPerBag.Name: Rate: handfuls per bag
handfulsPerBag.Hint: How many handfuls make one bag. In The Mist Age: 100 Silver = 1 Gold.

bagsPerChest.Name: Rate: bags per chest
bagsPerChest.Hint: How many bags make one chest. In The Mist Age: 10 Gold = 1 Gold Bar.

MIST_AGE_WEIGHT.WeightHint: Small 0-1, medium 2-3, large 4-8. Fractions allowed. Leave empty for the default ({default}).
MIST_AGE_WEIGHT.LoadTooltip: Strength {strength}: {capacity} slots{bonus}. Up to {free} slots over capacity is light overload; beyond that, heavy overload.
MIST_AGE_WEIGHT.LoadTooltipNoStrength: No Strength: base capacity {capacity} slots{bonus}. Up to {free} slots over capacity is light overload; beyond that, heavy overload.
MIST_AGE_WEIGHT.LoadTooltipManual: Capacity set by hand: {capacity} slots{bonus}. Up to {free} slots over capacity is light overload; beyond that, heavy overload.
MIST_AGE_WEIGHT.CapacityHint: Capacity in slots. Leave empty for the formula ({default}).

FreeOverload.Name: Light overload limit
FreeOverload.Hint: How many slots over capacity count as light overload, a warning. Beyond that the character is heavily overloaded.

CharacterCapacity.Name: Carrying limit for characters
CharacterCapacity.Hint: When off, characters have no maximum load: their load is still counted in slots, but there is no capacity, bar or overload. Adversaries keep their limit.

MIST_AGE_WEIGHT.LoadUnlimitedTooltip: No carrying limit for characters: the load is only counted.

OverloadEffect.Name: Overload effect on characters
OverloadEffect.Hint: An overloaded character gets an effect on its token and sheet: one look for light overload, another for heavy. It carries the penalties set below. Off removes the effect and its penalties.

CharacterManualCapacity.Name: Players set character capacity by hand
CharacterManualCapacity.Hint: When on, a character's carrying capacity becomes an input in its load bar for whoever owns the sheet. An empty field uses the Strength formula. When off, the formula is always used.

CapacityBase.Name: Base capacity
CapacityBase.Hint: Slots a character with Strength 0 can carry.

CapacityPerStrength.Name: Slots per point of Strength
CapacityPerStrength.Hint: Added for every point of Strength above 0.

CapacityPerNegativeStrength.Name: Slots lost per negative point
CapacityPerNegativeStrength.Hint: Removed for every point of Strength below 0.

CharacterCapacityGMOnly.Name: Only the GM sets character capacity
CharacterCapacityGMOnly.Hint: With manual character capacity on, only the GM can change it; players see the number.

OverloadIcon.Name: Light overload icon
OverloadIcon.Hint: Image of the light overload effect. Changing it updates the icons already shown.

OverloadHeavyIcon.Name: Heavy overload icon
OverloadHeavyIcon.Hint: Image of the heavy overload effect. Changing it updates the icons already shown.

OverloadLightEffect.Name: Light overload effect
OverloadLightEffect.Hint: What light overload does to a character, edited in the Daggerheart effect sheet: changes and conditionals. For a penalty add a change with Add and a negative value, e.g. system.evasion, Add, -1.

OverloadHeavyEffect.Name: Heavy overload effect
OverloadHeavyEffect.Hint: What heavy overload does to a character, instead of the light overload effect.

MIST_AGE_WEIGHT.EffectEditorMissing: This Daggerheart version has no effect sheet for settings; overload effects cannot be edited here.
